boundary_dependence.the identity of the policy space, the ca: does not depend on the admitted boundary
boundary_dependence.the invisibility of the nesting at every: requires the admitted boundary, being a statement about which side a mark lies on after the inner boundary is discarded or absorbed
boundary_dependence.the notion of depth, the address, the cr: require the admitted boundary: a crossing is a crossing OF a boundary, and an address is a sequence of its sides.  Nothing in this rung's state is formulated after removing it
boundary_dependence.the outside of the outermost boundary: requires the admitted boundary to be formulated at all, and the run formulates no address value for it; that is recorded OPEN
boundary_dependence.the reader's depth bound and the domain: require the admitted boundary in the weak sense that a whole is delimited by one bar with a side on each hand; how many items a side may carry and how deep the reader goes are declarations the boundary does not decide
boundary_dependence.the two senses of an available depth, an: does not depend on the admitted boundary: one is a statement about renamings and a key, the other about the forms of the closed observation grammar, and both would be stated the same way for any state carrying a sequence

admitted boundary.buys_at_challenge_5: that an item lies on a side at all, and therefore that a nested item lies on a side of a side; every policy but the refusing one is formulable only under it, and so is the whole notion of a crossing
admitted boundary.declared_at: the seed, as the one admitted primitive exception

occurrence identity.buys_at_challenge_5: that a presented item becomes a fresh admitted mark whatever labels are already present, which every admitting policy uses
occurrence identity.declared_at: Challenge 2, as that rung's one new declaration

presentation convention.buys_at_challenge_5: which presented side becomes which admitted side, now applied at every level; the run declares one convention for all levels and does not enumerate a policy that reads a different one inside

side names under O.buys_at_challenge_5: which side of the OUTER boundary the retained mark lies on, at every policy that admits it.  It buys nothing about the inner boundary: whether the naming reaches inward is a further declaration, and without it the inner side is not internally available under O either
side names under O.declared_at: genesis, as the O reading of the one declaration

the nested reader bound.buys_at_challenge_5: that the caller's inscription can be read at all, and a finite domain of inscriptions to enumerate; it decides nothing about what an admission does with what it reads

the widened reader bound.buys_at_challenge_5: nothing here: the Challenge 4 reader refuses the caller's inscription by name, exactly as the Challenge 1 reader does

domain.declared_because: two policies are the same policy exactly when they retain isomorphic states at every member of this domain; the domain is a declaration, and a wider alphabet or a deeper bound is available and is not enumerated

identity_policy_inherited: occurrence identity: an admission admits a fresh mark, the token being a label

measures.mu1: capability count: the number of undeclared capabilities the candidate uses
measures.mu2: collateral count: how many of the eight declared facts about the caller's retained whole the candidate makes internally available that the same reading's base did not.  The base is the refusing policy, which retains nothing, and a fact about a retained configuration is reported FALSE where there is no retained configuration rather than vacuously true.  The eight are facts and not independent facts: the receipt computes which pairs of them take the same value at every point of this rung's space and names them, so that a reader knows where this measure counts one thing twice

outside_of_the_outermost_boundary.note: an address is a sequence of sides crossed INWARD from the outermost boundary, and the declared alphabet has two values, both of them sides of a boundary already crossed.  There is no value for a place beyond the outermost boundary, and the run declares none: the question is named and left OPEN rather than answered by a declaration made to answer it

capability_of.admit_a_whole_as_a_mark: an admission event may name an item that is not a visible mark, and admit it as one mark on a side
capability_of.reach_inside_a_nested_whole: an admission event may name a mark lying inside a nested whole, so that the interior of an item is reachable at all
capability_of.record_the_crossing: the state records, for each admitted mark, the finite sequence of sides crossed to reach it rather than one side, and the event grammar gains the admission that names such a sequence
capability_of.the_reading_names_the_inner_sides: the reading's naming of the two sides reaches the inner boundary, so that the exchange of an inner boundary's two sides is not a renaming the object language can miss

policy_space.exhaustive_because: an admission meeting an item that is a whole either does not act on it (refuse), acts on the whole without its interior (opaque), acts on the interior without the boundary between (discard), or acts on the interior keeping that boundary (record).  Those four exhaust the declared alternatives; what the space does NOT enumerate is a policy that admits the inner whole AND its items as separate marks, one that admits the inner boundary as a datum of its own, one that reads an item under a different convention at each level, or one that groups marks by anything but the crossing.  Every minimality statement of this rung is scoped to the declared four
members: refuse: an admission never names an item that is a whole
opaque: the inner whole is admitted as ONE mark on the outer side and its interior is discarded
discard: the inner boundary is discarded and the inner whole's own items are admitted on the outer side
record: the inner whole's items are admitted, each carrying the finite sequence of sides crossed to reach it
policy_space.one_step_rule: a candidate is one step exactly when the number of undeclared capabilities it uses is one.  At Challenge 4 that number was also the number of coordinates moved; here it is not, the policy coordinate having a value that uses two capabilities, and the run keeps the capability reading because the seed requires a candidate called one step not to bundle capabilities

C4-X.evidence: both inherited readers refuse the caller's inscription by name and the third widening is paid by the run; the decision takes the form of a declared finite policy space of four members; depth is available at no policy of capability count one; and the inner whole is a second initial datum under no policy
C4-X.exactly_one_clause_fact: the frozen clause reads 'a declared finite space of policies with exactly one member letting the caller retain the inscription'.  THREE of the four declared policies admit the caller's inscription; exactly one retains it so that the retained state tells it from the flat inscription.  The clause is scored on the first count, which is what 'letting the caller retain the inscription' says, and the second is reported beside it
C4-X.label: NOT FORCED

C5-1.evidence: both inherited readers refuse the caller's inscription by name; the widened reader reads it as a whole whose left item is a whole and whose right side is empty, at depth two; and it refuses a whole deeper than its declared bound by name
C5-1.label: FORCED
C5-1.result_basis: DEFINITION-level: the two refusals are the Challenge 1 and Challenge 4 bounds replayed on the caller's text, and the widened reader's own bound is this rung's declaration; a hit is by construction and is not counted as content

C5-2.evidence: four declared policies at capability counts 0, 1, 1, and 2 over three declared capabilities; a policy is one step exactly when its capability count is one; and the recording policy, which is what the caller's demand needs, is refused as a bundle
C5-2.label: NOT FORCED
C5-2.result_basis: DEFINITION-level: the four policies, the three capabilities named for them, and therefore the counts and the identity of one step with capability count one are declarations of this rung; a hit is by construction and is not counted as content

C5-3.evidence: under both one-step policies and both readings the caller's inscription retains exactly one mark, and what it retains is isomorphic to what the Challenge 1 inscription retains, so the nesting is internally invisible there
C5-3.label: FORCED
C5-3.result_basis: content: the comparison with what `<a|>` retains is an isomorphism-witness search over the unpruned enumeration at each candidate's own renamings, and both values are attained elsewhere in the space

C5-4.evidence: the two one-step policies part on the declared domain and agree at the caller's own inscription; the minimum capability count among admitting points is one, two classes attain it, both are retained, and uniqueness is refuted under both readings
C5-4.label: FORCED
C5-4.result_basis: content: the separation of the two one-step policies is a census over the declared domain with the parting inscriptions named, and the class count is the implemented quotient

C5-5.evidence: no retained state under any policy carries a second initial datum; the inner whole is a mark under the opaque policy, nothing under the discarding policy, and a second boundary under the recording policy; and a further mark may be admitted inside it under the recording policy alone, which is not one step
C5-5.label: NOT FORCED
C5-5.result_basis: content: that no policy makes a second initial datum is a replay of every point's history with the datum read off, and that a further mark may be admitted within the inner whole is an event-acceptance probe with both values attained.  The classification of what the inner whole IS under each policy is the run's and is declared, not computed

C5-6.evidence: under every one-step policy every retained mark has depth one, so depth separates nothing; under the recording policy the domain holds depths one and two and equal keys give equal depths; and no form of the closed observation grammar reads depth at any point
C5-6.label: FORCED
C5-6.result_basis: content: the key-determination of depth is a census over the declared domain, and the depths a policy can hold are read off the same census.  That no form of the closed grammar reads depth is DEFINITION-level, the grammar being the declared sum of two forms, and it is reported separately

C5-7.evidence: the naming coordinate collapses at every policy under U and at three of four under O; the retained mark's address orbit has four members under U, one under O with the naming reaching inward, and two under O without it, so which side of the inner boundary the mark lies on is not internally available under O either without that further declaration
C5-7.label: FORCED
C5-7.result_basis: content: the collapse is the implemented quotient over the whole declared domain, and the orbit sizes are read off the unpruned enumeration of each candidate's permitted renamings

C5-8.evidence: at every point the initial datum and the reading are unchanged and the event-follows relation is empty on every probe of both grammars; every admitting point's history is certified and replays from genesis; and no rule of an earlier rung is withdrawn
C5-8.label: FORCED
C5-8.result_basis: content: the certification and the replay are computed at every point of the space, and both values of the admission predicate are attained.  That the event-follows relation is empty is the declared grammar and is DEFINITION-level

tally.criterion: a prediction counts as content only if at least one of its hitting clauses, read literally, rests on a theorem outside the DEFINITION-level lists of the paper's section 7 or on a computation not fixed by a declaration alone; a prediction whose every clause is true by unfolding a declaration, or reports a modelling decision of the run, is HIT by construction and not counted as content

what_the_challenge_exercises.admission: yes, and it is the rung's subject: what an admission does with an item that is a whole is the declared policy space, and no policy is taken
what_the_challenge_exercises.current-state designation: yes: every retained state is the replay of an explicit history, and the current configuration is the Challenge 4 retention, no policy of this rung having been taken
what_the_challenge_exercises.equality: yes: structural equality of a deep regime, the isomorphism relation at a candidate's permitted renamings, and the sameness of two POLICIES over the declared domain are three different relations, and the rung uses all three
what_the_challenge_exercises.mention: yes: the inner whole is named by the reader and by the refusal, and naming it is not admitting it
what_the_challenge_exercises.observation: yes: the closed grammar is unchanged and no form is added; the rung computes that no form of it reads depth
what_the_challenge_exercises.retention: yes: what the caller's retention amounts to is exactly what the policy space decides, and three of the four policies retain something
what_the_challenge_exercises.side: yes, and it is the rung's subject: a side of a side is what the caller's inscription presents, and only the recording policy keeps the difference between the two levels
what_the_challenge_exercises.supply: yes: one Supply per admitted mark, before every admission of the retained whole; a policy that admits nothing supplies nothing
